common_mistakes: Installing high-pile racks before the fire sprinkler evaluation is approved — the fire marshal can require changes or removal of installed racks
Submitting only a building permit and skipping fire protection review for rack storage over 12 feet
Failing to show rack anchorage and aisle widths on the plan set, which can stall plan review
Assuming the existing sprinkler layout is acceptable without verifying clearance and obstruction rules for the new rack configuration
Starting work before the permit is issued and posted at the job site

pro_tips: Bring a rack layout with exact storage heights and commodity type up front — that is what drives the sprinkler review and avoids a correction cycle.
If the warehouse is in a special district or has any zoning overlay, submit that information with the first package so the city does not kick it back for sub-record review.
Have the rack manufacturer's anchorage details ready before submittal; Tucson reviewers will want to see how the racks are fixed to the slab.
Use ACA to track corrections and resubmittals so you do not lose time waiting on email back-and-forth.
